result: __libc_freeres releases stream buffers and the calling thread's getpw*/netdb, resolver and dlerror state: memcheck shows 0 reachable bytes for puts, cxx and mix (was 4,104/4,104/5,080), as stock; gate red only on the 6 mei locale tests of incident #7846

gate.affected: 10828 passed / 12 failed (the 6 #7846 locale tests, each failed twice; host locale archive replaced); conformance 27 passed / 0 failed

rulings.item: Reversal of ruling #1317 (inert __libc_freeres): it now releases library-allocated blocks (D-29.7; COMPAT-11 withdrawn)
rulings.recommendation: accept: checkers call it only at exit; a mid-run call keeps every stream's data; only the calling thread's earlier getpw*/netdb results become invalid, as their contract allows

informational: mei: gate and cargo xtask test fail catalogs_products, locale_data x2, locale_products, printf_corpus_products, s7_2_f_0 since locales-all replaced the locale archive (#7846, LOCALE-PER-DIR-LOAD); panics say 'the gate machines have a locale archive' or the reference's own setlocale fails; same 6 on the leg-2 gate and xtest

valgrind without libniji's libc6-dbg stops at start-up (mandatory strcmp redirect in ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 not found), before and after this change alike; already tracked by the VALGRIND-LDSO-SYMBOLS stories

impact.what: memcheck reachable at exit, puts / cxx / mix with libc6-dbg (valgrind 3.24, trixie root)

improvement: a gate whose only reds are a known host incident has no way to say so: a host-incident list (test names + incident id) the verifier subtracts would stop such stories going red and needing a continuation
next_step: land once mei's locale incident #7846 is fixed (LOCALE-PER-DIR-LOAD) or gate on another host; nothing left in the story
